examples.question_text: Plan a skeletal rectangular-prism model. How many straws and joiners are needed? Describe how to build it.
examples.solution_text:
Make two matching rectangular frames, using four straws and four joiners for each frame. Join corresponding corners with four more straws of equal length.

$\begin{align*}\text{Straws} &= 4+4+4 \\ &= 12 \\ \text{Joiners} &= 4+4 \\ &= 8\end{align*}$

Use 12 straws and 8 joiners. Each straw represents an edge and each joiner represents a vertex.

examples.question_text: Plan a skeletal triangular-pyramid model. How many straws and joiners are needed? Describe how to build it.
examples.solution_text:
Build a triangular base with three straws and three joiners. Add a straw from each base corner and connect their other ends at one apex joiner.

$\begin{align*}\text{Straws} &= 3+3 \\ &= 6 \\ \text{Joiners} &= 3+1 \\ &= 4\end{align*}$

Use 6 straws and 4 joiners.

It makes a cube, which is a square prism with six square faces.

Fold the four squares in the strip to form the sides. Fold the two attached squares to close the top and bottom, then tape the meeting edges.

It makes a square pyramid: one square base and four triangular side faces.

Fold each triangle upwards along a square edge. Bring the four outer triangle vertices together at the apex, then tape the meeting edges.

examples.question_text: A hexagonal-prism model has two matching hexagonal ends. List the rectangular face pieces needed to join the ends, and explain how to attach them.
examples.solution_text:
Each hexagon has six sides, so use six rectangular joining faces.

Attach one rectangle to each side of the first hexagon. Join neighbouring rectangles along their side edges, then attach the matching hexagon to the open end. The complete model has two hexagonal faces and six rectangular faces.

examples.question_text: A pentagonal-prism model has two pentagonal ends but only four rectangular side faces. A triangular-pyramid frame has four joiners but only five straws. Explain what each model is missing.
examples.solution_text:
The pentagonal prism needs one rectangular face for each of the five sides of its base. It is missing one rectangular side face.

The triangular pyramid needs three base edges and three edges to the apex: $3+3=6$ straws. Its four joiners are enough, but it is missing one straw edge.

examples.question_text: A complete prism frame uses 21 straws, with one straw for each edge. Determine its base shape and the number of joiners needed.
examples.solution_text:
For each side of one base, a prism has one edge in each of its two bases and one joining edge. Group the straws in threes.

$21\div3=7$

Each base has seven sides, so the model is a heptagonal prism.

There are seven vertices in each base: $7+7=14$ joiners.

examples.question_text: A complete pyramid frame uses 10 straws, with one straw for each edge. Determine its base shape and the number of joiners needed.
examples.solution_text:
A pyramid has one base edge and one edge to the apex for each base side. Group the straws in pairs.

$10\div2=5$

The base has five sides, so the model is a pentagonal pyramid.

There are five base vertices and one apex: $5+1=6$ joiners.

Build a square pyramid. The square top view shows the base outline and four edges meeting above its centre. The triangular front and side views show the apex above the base.

Use one square base and four matching triangular side faces. Attach a triangle to each base edge, then bring their outer vertices together at the apex.

examples.derivation: Two rectangular frames require 4+4=8 edges and 4+4=8 vertices. Four corresponding-corner connections give 8+4=12 edges. Therefore 12 straws and 8 joiners are needed; the construction produces a rectangular prism.
A triangular base has three edges and three vertices. Three edges connect those vertices to one apex, giving 3+3=6 edges and 3+1=4 vertices. Therefore 6 straws and 4 joiners are needed.

The diagram contains four equal squares in a strip and two more attached on opposite sides of the second square. Folding the strip forms four side faces; the attached squares close opposite ends without overlap. The resulting six-square solid is a cube, a particular square prism.

The square has side length 2 diagram units. Each attached triangle has base 2 and altitude approximately 1.7320508, so its other sides are also 2. These four equilateral triangles fold into a square pyramid: the centre-to-base-corner distance is sqrt(2), and apex height sqrt(2) gives apex-to-corner edges of length 2. There are one square and four triangular faces.

Each of the six sides of a hexagonal end requires one rectangular joining face. Six rectangles and two matching hexagons form the eight faces of the prism. The stated assembly joins neighbouring rectangles and closes the remaining end.

A pentagonal prism requires five rectangular side faces; 5-4=1 is missing. A triangular pyramid requires three base edges plus three apex edges, giving six straws; 6-5=1 straw is missing. Its three base vertices and apex require exactly four joiners.

A prism has equally many edges in its first base, second base and joining set. Dividing 21 by 3 gives seven sides per base, identifying a heptagonal prism. Two sets of seven base vertices require 14 joiners.
A pyramid has equally many base edges and apex edges. Dividing 10 by 2 gives five base sides, identifying a pentagonal pyramid. Five base vertices plus the apex require six joiners.

The top view shows a square outline with four corner-to-centre apex-edge projections. The centred triangular front view and matching side view are consistent with a square pyramid whose apex is above the base centre. It is constructed from one square base and four matching triangular side faces.
